content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I attempted to measure feedback time using a Stopwatch function as shown in the attached example. Can someone assist me with integrating a comparator to check the time difference between each Stopwatch instance? If the difference between the two Stopwatch readings surpasses 50ms, I want it to indicate a failure. Thank you in advance.
You could use three analog comparators, correct?

The Stopwatch’s measured value is 32 bits wide (DWord), but the analog comparator handles only 16-bit inputs. If the time value goes beyond 32,767, the Stopwatch keeps running, but the analog comparator stops at 32,767. So, using a simple analog comparison works only if the value stays below 32,767.

Hello. Does anyone else share concern about the 50ms difference? I previously attached an idea: the left side was a test concept and the right side a comparison suggestion. The approach wasn’t suitable and the attachment has been removed. Apologies for any inconvenience.
Hi! Thank you, this is sufficient for my needs. Could you send me the program (with the comparator settings) for reference? Thanks again.
Hello [user_name], Here’s an idea if you want to experiment with comparator functions.

Your settings for the comparators are incorrect. The minimum time unit for the Stopwatch is 1/100s, not 1/1000s. If you click on the block, you’ll see 1/100s as the base value. Although the block is labeled as "ms", 1 unit is actually 10ms. Therefore, you need to enter 5, not 50, into the comparator; the circuit works only if the measured time doesn’t exceed 5 minutes, 27 seconds, and 67 hundredths. Also, similar to other users, I’m skeptical whether a minimum resolution of 1/100s can precisely capture a 5/100s time difference.
Thank you all, this discussion has been very helpful for me.

Hello. Please clarify a couple of points from your previous example (thanks for sharing!). What is the function of amplifiers labeled B29, B30, and B31? How is a difference window of -50ms and +50ms managed? Thanks in advance.

analysis.insight_summary: The original poster is trying to compare time differences between two Stopwatch functions and trigger a fault if the gap exceeds a certain threshold. The discussion identifies practical barriers: the hardware/software analog comparator’s 16-bit limit compared to the Stopwatch’s 32-bit value, and the Stopwatch’s resolution of only 1/100s, making it tricky to measure short intervals exactly. Participants suggest various concepts and clarify implementation details, but agree on the constraints and do not provide a straightforward, functioning solution.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for an accurate and dependable method to compare time measurements from Stopwatch functions—alerting when the time gap crosses a specified threshold (such as 50ms) and reliably flagging such cases.
